statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-116318 (PostgreSQL pg_dump not-null constraint name allows SQL injection) affects only PostgreSQL 18. The PostgreSQL security page, https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-116318/, says versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected and lists 18.7 as the only fixed release, and the CVE record, https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-116318, lists only major version 18 as affected. The flaw is in how pg_dump prints the name of a child table's own NOT NULL constraint on an inherited column. Named NOT NULL constraints exist only from PostgreSQL 18, which stores column NOT NULL specifications in pg_constraint, as the PostgreSQL 18 release notes say: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.0/. The fix, https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/d7344264584bd66ff4dcb038c6f57e773b8abc3a, quotes that name in src/bin/pg_dump/pg_dump.c and is marked back-patch through 18. At every PostgreSQL 16 release this owner publishes (REL_16_13 through REL_16_16), pg_dump.c tracks no per-column NOT NULL constraint names and prints a column's NOT NULL without a constraint name; see for example https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/REL_16_16/src/bin/pg_dump/pg_dump.c. The pg_dump program in every published DHI postgresql16-client build for Alpine 3.23 (16.13-r0, 16.14-r0, 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0), on both x86_64 and aarch64, reports its 16.x release and does not contain the "CONSTRAINT %s NOT NULL" format string that PostgreSQL 18's pg_dump uses for named NOT NULL constraints, which the postgresql18-client 18.7-r0 pg_dump does contain on both architectures. None of the Alpine patches applied in the 16.16-r0 APKBUILD touch pg_dump. The 16.16 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/16.16/, do not list this CVE. Alpine's postgresql16 16.16-r0 secfixes list CVE-2026-116318, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/859fa0795e895af033fab32094a83301f2b4d8ff/community/postgresql16/APKBUILD, but upstream's own advisory places PostgreSQL 16 outside the affected range.

statements.status_notes: PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-116318 (PostgreSQL pg_dump not-null constraint name allows SQL injection) in 18.7: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-116318/ lists 18.7 as the fixed release for major version 18, and the 18.7 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.7/, list this CVE. The security page says versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected, so this owner's 18.x builds are in scope. The fix is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/9e4cde7927da3603a2b6ca0d4e75d50b28888252 on the REL_18_STABLE branch, which changes src/bin/pg_dump/pg_dump.c (plus its TAP test) so that pg_dump quotes not-null constraint names with fmtId(); it is tagged Security: CVE-2026-116318 and Backpatch-through: 18; it is in the REL_18_7 release tag and not in REL_18_6. The DHI postgresql18 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql18 APKBUILD, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/59a1f1d230675807d5a95a0c1e57ba5d640ba039/main/postgresql18/APKBUILD, which builds the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball; none of the patches it applies touch the files this fix changes. We checked the pg_dump program, /usr/libexec/postgresql18/pg_dump, in every published postgresql18-client package for Alpine 3.23 on both x86_64 and aarch64 (checksums verified against the package index): 18.7-r0 reports PostgreSQL 18.7 and carries the fix, while the earlier builds 18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0 and 18.6-r0 report 18.1, 18.2, 18.3, 18.4 and 18.6 and are affected. As a check, the format string the fix removes ("CONSTRAINT %s NOT NULL %s") is present in the pg_dump binary of 18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0 and 18.6-r0 and absent from 18.7-r0 on both architectures. 18.7-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix. Alpine's postgresql18 APKBUILD lists CVE-2026-116318 under its 18.7-r0 secfixes.
